rules.title: SQL built with %, format() or an f-string
rules.why: DB-API parameter substitution exists precisely so query text is never built from values. String building here is injectable.
rules.falsePositiveHints: cursor.execute(sql, params) with a tuple/dict is the safe form. An f-string that only inserts a validated table name from an allow-list is lower severity but still worth noting.

rules.title: Django ORM raw SQL or extra()
rules.why: raw() and extra() drop out of the ORM's parameterization; extra() is deprecated partly for this reason.
rules.falsePositiveHints: raw() with the params= argument is parameterized and safe.

rules.title: Subprocess or OS command with shell semantics
rules.why: shell=True with any interpolated value lets the caller chain commands with ; or |.
rules.falsePositiveHints: subprocess.run(["prog", arg]) with a list and shell=False is safe. A fully literal command with shell=True is Info.

rules.title: Unsafe deserialization
rules.why: Unpickling attacker-controlled bytes executes arbitrary code by design.
rules.falsePositiveHints: yaml.safe_load is safe. yaml.load with Loader=SafeLoader is safe. Pickling to and from a trusted local cache is lower risk but still worth a note.

rules.title: Dynamic code evaluation
rules.why: eval/exec over request-influenced strings is remote code execution.
rules.falsePositiveHints: exec in build/setup scripts and eval over literals are Info. ast.literal_eval is safe.

rules.title: Django DEBUG enabled or ALLOWED_HOSTS wide open
rules.why: DEBUG=True in production exposes settings, SQL, environment variables and a full traceback console to any visitor.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Fine in a settings/dev.py that production never loads, or when read from an environment variable. Check how settings are selected.

rules.title: Django SECRET_KEY hard-coded
rules.why: The SECRET_KEY signs sessions, CSRF tokens and password-reset links. Knowing it means forging all three.
rules.falsePositiveHints: os.environ / django-environ lookups are correct. A literal committed key is a Critical finding and requires rotation, not just removal.

rules.title: CSRF protection bypassed on a view
rules.why: csrf_exempt on a state-changing view allows cross-site invocation by any page the victim visits.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Legitimate on webhook receivers that verify a signature instead. Check for that verification.

rules.title: No authentication or permission enforcement detected
rules.why: No authentication decorators, mixins or dependencies anywhere means the routes are anonymous.
rules.falsePositiveHints: DRF DEFAULT_PERMISSION_CLASSES or global middleware also satisfies this - search settings before reporting.

rules.title: Jinja/Flask template rendered from a string
rules.why: Server-side template injection in Jinja reaches Python objects and commonly escalates to RCE. The |safe filter disables escaping.
rules.falsePositiveHints: |safe over content produced by a trusted sanitizer is acceptable. A template string with no interpolation is not a finding.

rules.title: Filesystem path or archive extraction without validation
rules.why: os.path.join with an absolute or ../ segment silently escapes the base directory; extractall trusts archive entry names.
rules.falsePositiveHints: send_from_directory performs its own check and is generally safe. Closed when the resolved path is verified against the base with os.path.realpath + startswith.

rules.title: Declared dependencies to inventory for advisory checking
rules.why: Collects the dependency inventory for the Step 4 advisory check.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Unpinned dependencies (no version specifier) are themselves a supply-chain finding under A08.
